description: Key Hansard speeches from MAID C-14 and C-7 debates, flagged for still-sitting MPs where present.

rows.speaker: Luc Thériault
quotes: Does she believe it is acceptable and humane for a person to have to go on a hunger strike to be able to access medical assistance in dying?

rows.speaker: Arif Virani
rows.role: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister of Justice
quotes: I am really disappointed, to be frank, to see my colleagues across the aisle delaying the bill, increasing the chances that the government misses the court-imposed deadline and prolongs the suffering of Canadians.
We know that the majority of Canadians believe that MAID is a basic human right.
The eligibility criterion requiring a reasonably foreseeable natural death would be repealed.
I am very disheartened to see members of the Conservative Party of Canada continue their delay tactics to slow this legislation.
Prolonging the suffering of Canadians is not in any of our interests and that is exactly what will transpire if the December 18 deadline is missed.
This period of 90 days is not a waiting period or a reflection period.

rows.speaker: Cathy McLeod
quotes: I heard this from 100% of the people in my riding, is that there should be very clear and specific language on the protection of the health conscience rights of our health care providers.
Last night, we turned down what I thought was a very reasoned amendment.

rows.speaker: Garnett Genuis
quotes: When all of the representative organizations who represent people with disabilities are raising big concerns, I think the government should take that seriously.
The Conservatives wanted the House to be able to sit in May and June. The Liberal government chose not to allow the House to sit.

rows.speaker: Gérard Deltell
quotes: Since this issue is literally about life or death, would it not have been better to have the Supreme Court of Canada as the court to rule definitively on this issue?

rows.speaker: Jody Wilson-Raybould
rows.role: Minister of Justice and Attorney General of Canada
quotes: Bill C-14 represents the government's policy choice to address medical assistance in dying, a choice that is fully informed by consultations with Canadians and experts.

An assisted death could be an acceptable treatment for a soldier with post-traumatic stress disorder, a young person who suffered a spinal cord injury in an accident, or a survivor whose mind was haunted by memories of sexual abuse.
Under an approach where any serious medical condition is eligible, the law would be saying that an assisted death could be an acceptable treatment for a soldier with post-traumatic stress disorder.
The eligibility criterion requiring a reasonably foreseeable natural death would be repealed.
While the Carter decision told us that an absolute prohibition in the former law went too far, it did not tell us how medical assistance in dying should be implemented.
I call on all members of the House to support Bill C-14.

rows.speaker: John Barlow
quotes: There is no funding in the 2016 budget for palliative care. We tried to put an amendment through last night, which was voted down.
What is the long-term plan for palliative care?

rows.speaker: Mark Warawa
quotes: 84% of Canadians do support this under certain criteria, and that criteria is that the illness is terminal, and the person is suffering terribly and repeatedly asks to have assisted suicide to end their suffering.
70% of physicians in Canada do not want to be a part of this. They do not want to be forced through coercion, intimidation, or threats.
A young medical student asked me if physicians were going to be forced to do this and I said that there is a good possibility.
Physicians across this country are going to refuse to participate, saying they are now of retirement age and will retire or will relocate to another jurisdiction.
A shortage of physicians and nurses will create a medical emergency in Canada.

rows.speaker: Maryam Monsef
quotes: moved that Bill C-7, An Act to amend the Criminal Code (medical assistance in dying), be read the third time and passed.

rows.speaker: Randall Garrison
quotes: COVID was partially responsible for the delay, but certainly the Liberal government's prorogation was a bigger cause for the delay.
What are the consequences for Quebec and for the rest of the country if we do not meet this deadline?

rows.speaker: Rob Moore
quotes: Not one of the amendments that were proposed by our Conservative Party at committee was adopted.
Krista Carr, executive vice-president of Inclusion Canada, a group that represents persons with disabilities, said that Bill C-7 represents the 'worst nightmare' for persons with disabilities.

Why did they not listen to the persons with disabilities community and why is he talking about delays, when it was his government that prorogued the House and caused Bill C-7 to have to have a complete restart.
